findings.issue_text: Adding abstract order() to CryptoProvider breaks binary compatibility with existing third-party implementations, causing AbstractMethodError during provider detection; it should be a default method.

CryptoIntegration silently resolves same-priority providers by ServiceLoader iteration order; with default and FIPS providers both at priority 200, this can nondeterministically select non-FIPS crypto instead of failing fast.
ASN1Decoder accepts indefinite-length DER (0x80) as -1; for INTEGER values read(-1) throws NegativeArraySizeException rather than rejecting malformed ASN.1 with IOException.

goldens.comment: Returns wrong provider (default keystore instead of BouncyCastle)

Dead code exists where ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded. The actual encoding is performed by new ASN1Encoder instances created in the subsequent return statement, rendering the earlier operations useless.
When length starts at -1 from indefinite-length encoding, the arithmetic 'length = length - bytes.length' will behave unexpectedly, potentially leading to incorrect processing of encoded data.
Abstract order() method on CryptoProvider may break backward compatibility with existing implementations

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: Returns wrong provider (default keystore instead of BouncyCastle)
per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: CryptoIntegration silently resolves same-priority providers by ServiceLoader iteration order; with default and FIPS providers both at priority 200, this can nondeterministically select non-FIPS crypto instead of failing fast.
per_golden_matches.reasoning: Both comments identify the same underlying issue: when providers have the same priority (200), the wrong provider gets selected. The golden comment specifically says 'default keystore instead of BouncyCastle' is returned, while the candidate says 'non-FIPS crypto instead of failing fast' due to ServiceLoader iteration order. Both are pointing to the same bug where the provider selection mechanism incorrectly chooses the default provider over the intended one (BouncyCastle/FIPS) when priorities are equal.

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: When length starts at -1 from indefinite-length encoding, the arithmetic 'length = length - bytes.length' will behave unexpectedly, potentially leading to incorrect processing of encoded data.
per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: ASN1Decoder accepts indefinite-length DER (0x80) as -1; for INTEGER values read(-1) throws NegativeArraySizeException rather than rejecting malformed ASN.1 with IOException.
per_golden_matches.reasoning: Both comments identify issues related to indefinite-length encoding where length is -1. The golden comment points out that arithmetic operations with length=-1 will behave unexpectedly (length = length - bytes.length). The candidate comment identifies that when length is -1 (from indefinite-length 0x80), reading with that negative value causes a NegativeArraySizeException. These are related issues stemming from the same root cause (improper handling of -1 length from indefinite-length encoding), but they focus on slightly different manifestations - the golden focuses on the arithmetic subtraction behavior, while the candidate focuses on the array size exception when reading. They're pointing to the same underlying problem of not properly handling the -1 length value.
